Plot Method for Sequential Analysis Summaries

Source: R/plot.simsummary_fast.R
plot.simsummary_fast.Rd

Draws the stopping probabilities of a simsummary_fast result by look. With what = "cumulative" (default) one panel shows, for every block (arm or population), the cumulative probability of stopping for efficacy, which at the final look is the rejection rate, and, when futility boundaries were applied, the cumulative probability of stopping for futility. With what = "stage" each block has a panel of stacked bars of the probabilities of stopping for efficacy and for futility at each look.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'simsummary_fast'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("cumulative", "stage"),
  xaxis = c("look", "events", "time"),
  col = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  legend_pos = "topleft",
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object of class "simsummary_fast" from simsummary_fast.

what

"cumulative" (default) for the cumulative stopping probabilities of all blocks in one panel, or "stage" for the stopping probabilities at each look, one panel per block.

xaxis

The horizontal axis: "look" (default), "events", or "time". See Details.

col

Colors of the blocks, recycled. Defaults to a qualitative palette.

ylim

Limits of the vertical axis. Defaults to the range from 0 to slightly above the largest probability drawn.

legend_pos

Keyword giving the legend position, passed to legend.

xlab, ylab, main

Axis labels and title. Defaults depend on what and xaxis; with what = "stage" and several blocks, the panels are titled by their blocks.

...

Further arguments, currently ignored.

Value

The input x, invisibly.

Details

The plot uses the look rows of each block, which must keep all the looks of the design in their original order: a selection of rows or columns that the print method prints as an ordinary data frame (see print.simsummary_fast) gives an error. The cumulative probability of stopping for futility is the cumulative sum of prob.stop.futility over the looks.

The looks are placed on the horizontal axis by their index (xaxis = "look"), by the expected number of events at the look ("events", the column n.event.mean), or by the expected calendar time of the look ("time", the column cutoff.mean).

See also

simsummary_fast, print.simsummary_fast.

Examples

df <- simdata_fast(
  nsim     = 200,
  n        = c(150, 150),
  a.time   = c(0, 12),
  a.rate   = 300 / 12,
  e.hazard = list(0.05, 0.035),
  seed     = 1
)
res <- analysis_fast(df, control = 1, event.looks = c(60, 105, 150),
                     stat = c("logrank", "coxph"), side = 1)
oc <- simsummary_fast(res,
                      eff.col = "logrank.z",
                      efficacy = c(NA, -2.96, -1.97),
                      fut.col = "cox.coef",
                      futility = c(log(1.2), NA, NA),
                      direction = "lower")
plot(oc)

plot(oc, what = "stage", xaxis = "events")
